Problem: Given that the domain of f(x) is R, y=f(2x-1) is an odd function, and y=f(x+1) is an even function, and knowing that f(x)=e^x when x∈(-1,1), calculate the value of f(194). Express your answer as a single numerical value.

<reflection>
f is defined on all real numbers. From g(x)=f(2x-1) being odd: f(-2x-1) = -f(2x-1) for all x. From h(x)=f(x+1) being even: f(-x+1) = f(x+1) for all x. Substituting x=t-1 into the even-property equation gives f(2-t)=f(t), i.e. f(2-x)=f(x) for all x. Substituting x=2t-1 into the odd-property equation gives f(-x-2)=-f(x) for all x. The known interval value is f(x)=e^x for x in (-1,1). Using f(2-x)=f(x) at x=194 and x=-192 gives f(194)=f(-192) and f(-192)=f(194), which is only an identity.
Reflection symmetry f(2-x)=f(x) does not imply translation periodicity f(x+2)=f(x); applying the reflection twice simply returns the original argument, giving no new information.
Combine Equation A with Equation B to derive a translation relation (for example, substitute x -> -x-2 into Equation A or apply Equation B twice), then reduce f(194) modulo the resulting period into the known interval (-1,1).
</reflection>
